scope.objective: Reconstruct a bounded long task's Task Contract, plan progress, exact verifier state, trajectory phase, recovery decision, handoff, and next safe action in a new runtime process while failing closed on ambiguous durable state.

productionTree.canonicalization: UTF-8 sorted production paths from the FS0 constitution; JSON array of {path,mode,size,sha256}; aggregate SHA-256 is domain plus canonical JSON bytes

preArtifactWorkingTreeObservation.disposition: Dirty user-owned development tree retained. Exact production identity is local implementation evidence only; no clean or frozen release candidate is claimed.

authorities: Task Contract v2 remains the sole task, goal, scope, plan, acceptance, exact-verifier, and terminal authority.
The hash-chained task journal supplies durable checkpoints, retry ceilings, migration barriers, and interruption history.
The trajectory store supplies the exact lifecycle phase and blocks corrupt, mismatched, or unsafe transitions.
The handoff projection remains a bounded derived recovery view and never replaces the Task Contract.
reconstructionContract.freshProcess: session_start reconstructs the exact task/run/session identity and RuntimeSessionState delivers one bounded resume context at the first agent-start boundary only.
reconstructionContract.resumeContext: The deterministic resume context is capped at 6000 characters and includes bounded goal, expected output, acceptance focus, scope, work-plan progress, current checkpoint, current/stale verifier state, exact commands, next safe action, and handoff guidance without a follow-up provider turn.
reconstructionContract.nextAction: Terminal, unsafe, paused, retry, stale/current verifier, open-plan, and completion states map to one closed next-action vocabulary. A source task resumed in verify without current stable proof must run every exact configured verifier before continuing an open plan step.
reconstructionContract.delivery: Resume context is task/run/session bound and delivered at most once per runtime process; a later task or digest migration clears only the process-local delivery marker.

durabilityContract.journal: Every append is fsynced. An in-process append/fsync failure rolls back to the last valid byte boundary. A process-torn final segment without the writer's mandatory newline is ignored and truncated before the next append; newline-terminated malformed JSON remains corruption and blocks resume.
durabilityContract.handoff: Handoff writes use write, fsync, and atomic rename. ENOSPC, EACCES, or rename failure removes the partial temporary file and preserves the last authoritative handoff bytes.
durabilityContract.terminal: Completed, blocked, partial, and failed Task Contracts remain immutable and never recommend retry.
durabilityContract.privacy: All durable state stays under the existing private project-state boundary; the provider-visible resume projection omits raw session identity and remains bounded.

failureMatrix.case: process exit between execute and verify
failureMatrix.evidence: A fresh Node process reconstructs exact task/run identity, execute/verify progress, current step, current tree, and next action from disk.
Compaction preserves the Task Contract and checkpoint identity; the next runtime reconstructs the verifier phase without a second intake or context pack.
A non-newline final partial record is excluded, truncated at the prior valid boundary, and followed by one valid durable append.
Malformed committed-looking bytes remain visible corruption and force a bounded inspect-handoff path.
Injected ENOSPC and EACCES preserve the prior journal/handoff authority and leave no authoritative partial state.
External post-verify edits invalidate old proof; verify-phase resume without a current stable pass emits the exact configured verifier command before any open plan step.

failureMatrix.case: provider disconnect, verifier timeout, and retry exhaustion
failureMatrix.evidence: Recovery remains non-mutating, retry ceilings persist across processes, and exhausted tasks hand off without an extra continuation.
Symlinked or cross-identity handoff state fails closed instead of escaping the private state root.
